proof:
# One negative phase does not minimize its variance ratio at an endpoint

Consider four independent unit-rate exponentials and the proper section
with raw coefficients

    c(s)=(1,2,-2,-s), s>0.

Let F(s)=Pr(c(s) dot Y>=0), mu_i(s)=E(Y_i|c(s) dot Y=0), and

    R(s)=product_i mu_i(s)/[F(s)(1-F(s))].

Then

    R(1)=100/81 < R(0)=5/4,
    R(1)=100/81 < lim_(s->infinity)R(s)=245/192.    (1)

Thus a coordinatewise argument that tries to send each negative phase
to zero or infinity while never increasing the all-coordinate variance
ratio is false. This does not refute the variance inequality itself;
every ratio in (1) exceeds one.

At s=1, the actual quadrilateral section formulas give

    mu=(5/6,2/3,2/3,5/6), F=1/2,

so the ratio is 100/81. At s=0, the zero variable remains independent
with mean one and the remaining singleton-negative section has

    mu=(2/3,1/2,5/6,1), F=2/3.

This gives 5/4 exactly. The formulas are continuous as s decreases to
zero; the zero coefficient is treated as an independent variable, not
discarded from the product.

For the other endpoint put W=Y_0+2Y_1-2Y_2. Its cap probability is
P=2/3. Direct differentiation of
P(p,q,r)=1-r^2/[(p+r)(q+r)] at (p,q,r)=(1,2,2), or integration by parts,
gives the actual cap conditional means

    E((Y_0,Y_1,Y_2)|W>0)=(7/6,5/4,7/12).

Conditioning the large negative phase as in the entropy boundary source
gives

    lim R(s)=[(7/6)(5/4)(7/12)]/(2/3)=245/192.

The exact positive differences in (1) are respectively 5/324 and
215/5184. All entries come from actual exponential section or cap laws;
no independent moment menu or numerical realization is used.
